author: rroelke
body:
We are occasionally seeing the following failure in CI:
```
106: FATAL TileDB core library internal error: total_counter_.fetch_add(0) == 0 && "MemoryTracker destructed with outstanding allocations."
106:   tiledb/common/memory_tracker.cc:192
```
This assert failing indicates that we have some memory resource which is allocating memory but not freeing it.  However, we receive no guidance as to what entity might be responsible for that.

This pull request adds a `passert_failure` callback which dumps the memory tracker state to `stderr` if this assertion fails.  This way we will have a little more information the next time it fails.

Here's an example output from this assertion failing in a rapidcheck test:
```
FATAL TileDB core library internal error: total_counter_.fetch_add(0) == 0 && "MemoryTracker destructed with outstanding allocations."
  tiledb/common/memory_tracker.cc:192
LAST RAPIDCHECK INPUT:
(200, 8, 2, [], ???
)
MEMORY REPORT:
{"by_type":{"FilteredData":0,"FilteredDataBlock":0,"ParallelMergeControl":0,"QueryCondition":0,"ResultTileBitmap":0,"TileData":0,"TileHilbertValues":0},"total_memory":1,"tracker_id":"23","tracker_type":"QueryRead"}
```

author: jlowin
body: Deprecates the usage of e.g. `FastMCP.from_resource_fn()` in favor of always passing a Resource object to `FastMCP.from_resource()`. Naively, this looks like it adds code (having to create the resource object) but starts to let us carve away a birds nest of intertwined methods like FastMCP.from_resource_fn, ResourceManager.from_resource_fn, Resource.from_resource, etc, etc with no clear best practice. We will be explicit throughout the SDK and reserve helpful sugar for the core decorators.

body:
This let users decide if they prefer using exceptions or monads.

There's been a slight challenge due to the transactions. Currently the return type is the same as the callable being executed. 

But now the transactions errors are also returned meaning users now are forced to handle them. This will further incite them to abstract the call to `transactional` in a code of their own to centralize the way they want to deal with these errors (meaning either exceptions or inside monads).

> # Test Coverage Plan for PR34: Phase 5 Async Event Bus
> 
> ## Overview
> This document summarizes the current test coverage status and provides a concrete plan to reach >90% coverage for all new and changed code in PR34 (`codex/implement-phase-5-async-event-bus`).
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 1. Changed/New Files (from diff)
> - `cmd/eventdispatcher/main.go` (new)
> - `cmd/proxy/main.go`, `cmd/proxy/server.go` (changed)
> - `internal/eventbus/eventbus.go` (changed), `internal/eventbus/eventbus_test.go` (new)
> - `internal/eventtransformer/decode.go`, `openai.go`, `snakecase.go`, `tokens.go`, `transformer.go` (all new)
> - `internal/middleware/instrumentation.go` (changed)
> - `internal/server/server.go` (changed)
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 2. Coverage Gaps (from `go test -cover`)
> - **`internal/eventbus`**: Coverage below 90%. Needs more tests for all public methods and edge cases.
> - **`internal/eventtransformer`**: New files, almost no coverage. All exported functions need tests.
> - **`cmd/eventdispatcher` and `cmd/proxy`**: CLI entrypoints, almost no coverage. Add smoke and error-path tests.
> - **`internal/middleware/instrumentation.go`**: Changed, coverage status unclear—should be checked and improved if needed.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 3. Test Plan: What to Add/Improve
> 
> ### A. Event Bus (`internal/eventbus/eventbus.go`)
> - [ ] Test all public methods: `NewInMemoryEventBus`, `Publish`, `Subscribe`, `Stop`, `Stats`, `NewRedisEventBus`.
> - [ ] Test both in-memory and Redis event bus implementations.
> - [ ] Test edge cases: publishing with no subscribers, stopping the bus, error handling.
> 
> ### B. Event Transformer (`internal/eventtransformer/`)
> - [ ] `decode.go`: Test `DecompressAndDecode` for valid/invalid input, header variations.
> - [ ] `openai.go`: Test all exported functions (e.g., `IsOpenAIStreaming`, `MergeOpenAIStreamingChunks`, `TransformEvent`, etc.) for both happy path and error cases.
> - [ ] `snakecase.go`: Test `ToSnakeCaseMap` and `ToSnakeCase` with various input maps/strings.
> - [ ] `tokens.go`: Test `CountOpenAITokens` for different response types.
> - [ ] `transformer.go`: Test `DispatchTransformer` and any other exported logic.
> 
> ### C. CLI Entrypoints (`cmd/eventdispatcher/main.go`, `cmd/proxy/main.go`, `cmd/proxy/server.go`)
> - [ ] Add smoke tests for `main` functions (can use `os.Args` patching and subprocess testing).
> - [ ] Test error handling for missing/invalid arguments.
> - [ ] Test that help/version commands work and that main logic is invoked.
> 
> ### D. Middleware (`internal/middleware/instrumentation.go`)
> - [ ] Test `NewObservabilityMiddleware`, `Middleware`, and all methods on `captureResponseWriter`.
> - [ ] Test correct metrics/logging behavior and error handling.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 4. Prioritization
> 1. **Event Transformer**: All new, almost no coverage.
> 2. **Event Bus**: New logic, coverage still low.
> 3. **CLI Entrypoints**: No coverage, but easy to add basic tests.
> 4. **Middleware**: Ensure changes are covered.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 5. Next Steps
> - For each file above, enumerate all exported functions and ensure there is at least one test for each.
> - For CLI, add at least one test that invokes the main function with various arguments.
> - For event bus/transformer, add table-driven tests for all edge cases.
> - Re-run coverage after each batch of tests.
> 
> ---
> 
> *This plan is based on the latest diff with `main` and the output of `go test -cover`. Update this file as coverage improves or as new files/functions are added.*

body:
This PR implements the complete TaskRepository functionality as specified in issue #37, providing enhanced CRUD operations with proper entity relationships, concurrency handling, and hierarchical task management.

## Changes Made

### Enhanced CRUD Operations
- **GetByIdAsync**: Now includes Project, AssignedTo, and SubTasks with their relationships using efficient EF Core includes
- **UpdateAsync**: Added optimistic concurrency conflict handling with proper DbUpdateConcurrencyException management
- **DeleteAsync**: Implemented recursive cascade deletion for hierarchical task structures

### Key Features
- **Prevents N+1 queries** through strategic use of `Include()` and `ThenInclude()`
- **Handles task hierarchy** with proper parent-child relationships and recursive operations
- **Optimized performance** for hierarchical queries with minimal database round trips
- **Maintains data integrity** through proper cascade deletion of subtasks

### Example Usage
```csharp
// Get task with all related entities
var task = await taskRepository.GetByIdAsync(taskId);
// Returns task with Project, AssignedTo, and SubTasks loaded

// Update with concurrency handling
try {
    await taskRepository.UpdateAsync(modifiedTask);
} catch (DbUpdateConcurrencyException) {
    // Handle concurrency conflict
}

// Delete with cascade to subtasks
await taskRepository.DeleteAsync(parentTask);
// Recursively deletes all subtasks automatically
```

### Technical Implementation
- Used `new` keyword to enhance base Repository methods while maintaining interface compliance
- Added comprehensive unit tests with 100% coverage of new functionality
- Implemented proper Entity Framework includes to prevent N+1 query problems
- Added InternalsVisibleTo for unit testing of internal repository classes

### Quality Assurance
- **6 new unit tests** covering all scenarios including edge cases
- **All 190 existing tests still pass** - no breaking changes
- **Build succeeds** without errors or warnings
- **Proper error handling** for edge cases like non-existent tasks

The implementation satisfies all acceptance criteria:
✅ All CRUD operations implemented  
✅ Supports querying by project and assignee  
✅ Handles parent-child relationships  
✅ Includes related entities efficiently  
✅ Prevents N+1 queries  
✅ GetByIdAsync includes Project, AssignedTo, SubTasks  
✅ UpdateAsync handles concurrency  
✅ DeleteAsync cascades to subtasks  

Fixes #37.

author: adnv3k
body:
**Overview** This PR consolidates numerous improvements across the repository—ranging from dependency cleanup and icon additions to extensive UI refactoring, new session behaviors, and README updates. Below is a high-level summary of all changes: --- ## 1. Dependency Cleanup * **requirements.txt** * Removed redundant or unused packages to slim down dependencies. --- ## 2. New Assets * **ui/resources/icons/Play.png** (+226 KB) * Added a dedicated “Play” icon for pause/resume toggle in `SessionDisplay`. * **ui/resources/icons/brush.icns** * Included macOS icon to ensure proper toolbar icon on bundling. --- ## 3. Code Style & String Literal Unification * **GestureSesh.py**, **main\_window\.py**, **session\_display.py** * Replaced inconsistent string delimiters (single vs. double quotes) with a unified style. * Eliminated duplicate or dead code blocks and corrected minor bugs (e.g., duplicate assignments in `format_seconds`, `update_timer_display`). * Reformatted `if/else` conditions for clarity and removed commented‐out legacy code. --- ## 4. Global Styling & Font Handling * **main\_window\.py** +149 −40 * **session\_display.py** +4 −1 * Set Qt application style to **Fusion** for uniform look on Windows, macOS, and Linux. * In UI classes, replaced hardcoded fonts with platform-dependent fallbacks: ```python font.setFamily( "Apple SD Gothic Neo" if sys.platform == "darwin" else "Nanum Gothic" if sys.platform.startswith("win") else "Noto Sans CJK" ) ``` * Restyled background colors to dark‐mode friendly palettes (e.g., `rgb(24,43,59)` for session window, `rgb(30,56,78)` for image area). * Standardized all button stylesheets to `background: rgb(119,153,146);` or `background: rgb(100,120,118); padding:2px;` with consistent padding. --- ## 5. Button Initialization & Sizing * **GestureSesh.py** +196 −44 * Introduced `init_button_sizes()` to ensure every control button is exactly `60×36` (or `70×40` on macOS) with `32×32` icon size. * Added `init_buttons()` and `init_shortcuts()` to wire up click handlers and keyboard shortcuts in one place, replacing ad-hoc connections. --- ## 6. Shortcut & Tooltip Enhancements * **main\_window\.py**, **session\_display.py** * Restored the “Shift + Enter” shortcut for the “Add Entry” button in the main window. * Enhanced every tooltip to include both descriptive text and bolded shortcut hints (e.g., `“Pause Timer
Space”`). * Added new shortcuts in `SessionDisplay`: ``` Ctrl+O → Open image directory Ctrl+F → Toggle frameless window R → Toggle window resizing (dynamic/static) A → Toggle always-on-top M → Toggle mute Up → +30s Ctrl+Up → +60s Ctrl+Shift+Up → Restart timer Left/Right → Previous/Next image Esc → Stop session Space → Pause/Resume ``` --- ## 7. Review Mode & Image Directory Integration * **GestureSesh.py** +149 −40 * When a session ends, the window enters **Review Mode**: * Title changes to `“Review mode – closing in 15s (Ctrl+O opens folder)”`. * Arrow keys navigate through previously shown images. * Double-click or **Ctrl + O** opens the folder containing the current image and highlights the file (macOS: `open -R`, Windows: `explorer /select,`, Linux: `xdg-open`). * After 15 seconds of inactivity, the window closes automatically. Any key or mouse event cancels the close countdown. --- ## 8. Drag-to-Pause Behavior in `SessionDisplay` * **GestureSesh.py** +149 −40 * **session\_display.py** +70 −38 * Introduced a `drag_threshold = 6px` to distinguish between single-click (toggle pause/resume) and drag. * **`mousePressEvent`** * Record `old_position`, `drag_start_position`, and whether the timer was active (`was_timer_active`). * Reset `drag_timer_was_active = False`. * **`mouseMoveEvent`** * If cursor moves beyond threshold and the timer was running, **pause** the timer once and set a white border on the timer display. * Continue to drag the window while `drag_timer_was_active` is true. * **`mouseReleaseEvent`** * If a drag occurred (`drag_timer_was_active`), restore the timer to its prior state (`was_timer_active`). * Prevent unintended pause/resume from a single click when dragging. * Refactored `pause()`, `update_timer_display()`, and `_set_timer_visuals()` to cleanly toggle icons (`Pause.png` vs. `Play2.png`) and border styles. * Ensured single click on the image display toggles pause/resume only if movement is below threshold. --- ## 9. Timer Logic Refinements * **GestureSesh.py** +149 −40 * Consolidated countdown behavior: * If remaining time > 10 s and equals half of the scheduled time → play `halfway.mp3`. * If ≤ 10 s → play warning beep. * Simplified `update_timer_display()` to compute `hrs_list`, `minutes_list`, `sec` arrays once and call `display_time()`. * Eliminated redundant variable `secs`/`sec`. * In `restart_timer()`, reset `time_seconds` to current entry’s duration. --- ## 10. Session Completion & Close Countdown * **GestureSesh.py** +149 −40 * In `end_session()`: * Stop the timer, block further signals, set `close_seconds=15`, switch to Review Mode UI. * Reset indices so that previous/next navigation works from the last displayed image. * Start a separate `close_timer` (1 s interval) to decrement `close_seconds`. * On each tick, update the title bar via `update_close_title()`. When it reaches zero, close the window. * **`cancel_close_countdown()`** stops the close timer if the user interacts. --- ## 11. Break-Image Logic Corrections * **GestureSesh.py**, **main\_window\.py** * Rewrote `insert_breaks()` and `remove_breaks()` to use the new `ScheduleEntry` dataclass (fields: `images`, `time`). * Ensure that any entry with `images==0` inserts a `":/break/break.png"` at the correct index. * When skipping images, adjust break positions dynamically so that scheduled breaks remain aligned with entries. --- ## 12. Error Handling & Bug Fixes * **GestureSesh.py** * Fixed off-by-one in `format_seconds()` and `update_timer_display()`, removing duplicate assignments of `self.sec` vs. `self.secs`. * Corrected `load_entry(resume_timer)` to respect the previous timer state: * If `resume_timer=True`, timer resumes; otherwise it stays paused at the start of the new entry. * Guarded against `None` or corrupted images (checks for `cvimage is None or cvimage.size==0`). * Wrapped channel mismatch exceptions in `prepare_image_mods()` to gracefully report and skip invalid files. * Updated `skip_image()` to account for `break.png` and to move the break index by one if an image is skipped. * Removed unused methods and commented fragments such as legacy `skip_counter`. * **main\_window\.py** * In `check_files()` and `scan_directories()`, fixed string literal mismatches around `.jpeg` vs. uppercase/lowercase. * In `update_total()`, added exception logs for non-numeric table entries to avoid silent failures. * Ensured that `is_valid_session()` correctly checks `len(self.session_schedule)` and compares scheduled images to selected files. --- ## 13. UI Layout & XML Adjustments * **ui/main\_window\.ui** +2 −1 * Restored `Shift+Enter` under the “Add” button tooltip. * Cleaned up stray tags and aligned indentation. * **ui/resources/icons/Play.png** and **brush.icns** added to assets. --- ## 14. README Updates * **README.md** +32 −12 * Documented all new hotkeys, including **Review Mode** and **Open Image Folder (Ctrl + O)**. * Clarified that GestureSesh forces **Fusion** style to ensure dark-themed consistency. * Updated “Usage” s

author: yuya-takeyama
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: white-axe
body:
This pull request adds libretro builds to mkxp-z, which can be used in libretro frontends such as RetroArch.

Since RetroArch supports a lot of platforms, I was able to add support for a few extra platforms:

- Android
- Emscripten
- iOS
- Nintendo Switch
- PlayStation 4
- webOS

I've also added several other game console builds, but they don't work yet since they have no OpenGL support. I'll add a software renderer eventually for those consoles, but in the meantime, these non-functional console builds exist solely to make sure that no one breaks them.

Also, the libretro builds have save state support, which allows you to save and restore the state of the game engine whenever you want. Save states are 100% portable across different operating systems and CPU architectures; as for endianness, save states get saved in native endianness and the machine loading them performs byte swapping when loading if applicable. RetroArch's rewind feature is supported but requires disabling "Threaded Audio" in the core options because RetroArch doesn't support rewinding unless the audio is rendered from the main thread. Manual saving and loading of save states doesn't require disabling "Threaded Audio".

To try out a libretro build on a non-Emscripten, non-iOS platform, download the relevant core from the autobuild and put it wherever your libretro frontend keeps all the other cores. If you're using RetroArch and haven't updated your core info files in the RetroArch online updater since 2025-12-07, also use the online updater to update the core info files since that's around the time when I added the core info file for mkxp-z to RetroArch.

To test out the Emscripten build, I have it hosted at https://white-axe.github.io/mkxp-z-libretro-emscripten/.

For iOS, you need to manually build the frontend as described [here](https://docs.libretro.com/development/retroarch/compilation/ios/).

To run a game, you have several options:

- Load the Game.ini or mkxp.json as the game.
- Create an empty file with the file extension .rxproj, .rvproj or .rvproj2 in the same directory as Game.ini and/or mkxp.json, and load that as the game. This is intended to make it easier to deal with save states in RetroArch, since RetroArch's save states are named after the file you load as the game, so if you load Game.ini or mkxp.json, all the save states for every game will be named "Game" or "mkxp", which is really inconvenient.
- Put the game into a zip or 7z archive with file extension .mkxpz, .zip or .7z and load that as the game. Please note that the files inside the zip or 7z archive should be uncompressed if possible, especially .rgssad/.rgss2a/.rgss3a and .otf/.ttf files inside the archive, or the game will lag quite a bit from trying to seek compressed files.

There are a few differences between libretro builds and standalone builds:

- Every filesystem call made from Ruby is routed through a virtual filesystem with the following paths:
  - /Game - A directory with read-write permissions that represents the game directory, whatever RTPs the game uses, and the save directory all union mounted together (the save directory union mounting is for games that save to the current working directory). Files written to this path are always written to the save directory, not the game directory or RTP directories. The current working directory is always set to /Game when the game starts up.
  - /Save - A directory with read-write permissions that represents just the save directory without the union mounting with the game directory. The function `System.data_directory` returns "/Save/" in libretro builds.
  - /System/RTP - A directory with read-only permissions where RTPs are loaded from. This directory is physically located at \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/System/RTP.
  - /System/Fonts - A directory with read-only permissions where fonts are loaded from as a fallback if they aren't found in /Game/Fonts. This directory is physically located at \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/System/Fonts.
  - /System/Scripts/Preload - A directory with read-only permissions where preload scripts that can be selected in the core options are read from. This is the directory \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/Scripts/Preload. In addition, the three preload scripts provided in this repository are union mounted with it so that those preload scripts are usable without the user having to manually copy them here.
  - /System/Scripts/Postload - A directory with read-only permissions where postload scripts that can be selected in the core options are read from. This is the directory \<libretro system directory\>/mkxp-z/Scripts/Postload.
  - /Dist - A directory with read-only permissions that includes all the scripts and whatnot that Ruby needs to actually start up successfully. This directory is physically a zip file built during stage 1 of the libretro build, embedded in the libretro core and read directly from memory at runtime.
- RTP paths in mkxp.json are relative to /System/RTP instead of the game directory.
- RTPs set in Game.ini are loaded in libretro builds in addition to the ones specified in mkxp.json; they also get loaded from /System/RTP.
- The `System.platform` function always returns "libretro". All of the `System.is_` functions return false, except for a new `System.is_libretro?` function that returns true.
- The Ruby version has been changed to 3.3.10, because the build process used by the libretro cores is only supported by Ruby 3.2 and later and there are some bugs in the WASI builds of Ruby older than Ruby 3.3. I can change it to another version if you want, but it has to be at least 3.2.

A few things that I have yet to implement in the future:

- There are several console builds that don't work yet because they don't have OpenGL support. I'll eventually add a software renderer for those.
- ~~Loading preload scripts is not implemented yet. I'll likely attempt to use the libretro cheats interface to handle loading preload scripts.~~ Loading preload and postload scripts is now implemented. Any scripts in /System/Scripts/Preload or /System/Scripts/Postload can be enabled and disabled in the core options. Preload and postload scripts specified in mkxp.json will be loaded in addition to the ones specified in the core options; the preload scripts in mkxp.json will be loaded after the preload scripts specified in the core options, and the postload scripts in mkxp.json will be loaded before the postload scripts specified in the core options.
- Save states are currently unable to save and restore the positions of MIDI BGM tracks because seeking MIDI tracks is not implemented in the audio backend. I'll implement seeking for MIDI tracks to fix this.
- There is OpenGL support for the PlayStation Vita, but it requires all shaders to be written in a different language than GLSL. Other than that, though, everything else should be the same as normal OpenGL, so this most likely just needs a compiler that can convert the GLSL shaders to whatever format the Vita driver needs, or manual conversion of the shaders.
- Apparently, some devices that have PowerVR GPUs, in particular the PlayStation Vita but also some Android devices, have a limited number of OpenGL FBOs available. This is a problem, since mkxp-z uses one FBO per texture. I'll probably fix this by detecting if the device has a PowerVR GPU, and, if this is the case, changing the rendering to use a few global FBOs that are bound to textures when needed, and retaining the old method otherwise for better performance.
- I can also add builds for some Xbox consoles, which luckily have OpenGL support (via ANGLE). I'm pretty sure these require MSVC, though, so it might be tricky.

author: edpaget
body:
<!-- Added by 'Add Issue References to PR' GitHub Action. To disable linking, add 'no-auto-issue-links' label to your PR. --> helps with #58070

### Description

In https://github.com/metabase/metabase/pull/51929 we moved the collection permission check into a CTE to prevent it from being run multiple times to improve the performance of getting all the collections a user has permission to see. However we didn't move the effective-children subquery to use this cte since the query to get them needs to check the permissions of each 'effective' child as well are parents of the child collection to build this query. 

This separates out the effective child check from the permissions check so can we can use the permissions CTE inside the effective children query so we only perform permission checks once when loading items inside a collection.

- [ ] Tests have been added/updated to cover changes in this PR

This optimization improves memory throughput by using the aligned_vector struct to load 4 elements at a time, which should generate vectorized load instructions on the GPU. author: gabrielcoelho
body:
## 📖 Descrição

Esta PR implementa a configuração CORS global necessária para comunicação entre o backend Spring Boot (porta 8080) e frontend React+TypeScript (porta 5173/3000), além de uma aplicação de teste para validação.

## 🎯 Objetivos

- ✅ Permitir comunicação cross-origin entre frontend e backend
- ✅ Configuração escalável para futuros endpoints da API
- ✅ Ambiente de teste isolado para validação CORS
- ✅ Segurança adequada para ambiente de desenvolvimento

## 🔧 Alterações Realizadas

### Backend - Configuração CORS
- **Arquivo**: `src/main/java/br/com/cegonhaexpress/cegonha_express/config/CORSConfig.java`
- **Implementação**: `WebMvcConfigurer` com `addCorsMappings()`
- **Padrão de URLs**: `/api/**` (escalável para futuros endpoints)
- **Origens Permitidas**: 
  - `http://localhost:5173` (Vite padrão)
  - `http://localhost:3000` (porta alternativa)
  - `https://localhost:5173` e `https://localhost:3000` (SSL futuro)
- **Métodos HTTP**: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` (excluído `DELETE` por segurança)

### Aplicação de Teste
- **Localização**: `cors-test-app/`
- **Stack**: React + TypeScript + Vite
- **Porta**: 3000 (configurada no `vite.config.ts`)
- **Funcionalidade**: Teste visual da rota `GET /api/encomendas`
- **Interface**: EncomendaResponse tipada conforme DTO do backend

## 🧪 Como Testar

### Pré-requisitos
```bash
# Backend rodando
mvn spring-boot:run  # porta 8080

# Frontend de teste
cd cors-test-app
npm install
npm run dev  # porta 3000
```

### Cenários de Teste
1. **✅ CORS Funcionando**:
   - Acesse `http://localhost:3000`
   - Clique em "Buscar Encomendas"
   - Dados aparecem na tela
   - Console: "✅ CORS funcionou!"

2. **❌ CORS Bloqueado** (para comparação):
   - Comente a configuração no `CORSConfig.java`
   - Reinicie o backend
   - Teste novamente → erro CORS no console

## 🏗️ Decisões Arquiteturais

### Por que Configuração Global?
- ✅ **Escalabilidade**: Funciona automaticamente para novos controllers
- ✅ **Manutenibilidade**: Configuração centralizada
- ✅ **Simplicidade**: Adequado para projeto acadêmico
- ✅ **Flexibilidade**: Fácil de modificar conforme necessidades

### Por que Excluir DELETE?
- 🔒 **Segurança**: Operações destrutivas requerem autenticação
- 📚 **Escopo Acadêmico**: Foco em operações de leitura/criação
- 🚀 **Evolutivo**: Pode ser habilitado quando implementar autenticação

### Por que Múltiplas Portas?
- 🛠️ **Desenvolvimento**: Flexibilidade para equipe frontend
- 🔄 **Testes**: Diferentes ambientes de validação
- 📱 **Compatibilidade**: Suporte a diferentes ferramentas (Vite, CRA, etc.)

## 📊 Impacto

### Positivo
- ✅ **Desbloqueio**: Frontend pode consumir API
- ✅ **Produtividade**: Time frontend independente para desenvolvimento
- ✅ **Qualidade**: Validação automatizada via aplicação teste
- ✅ **Documentação**: Exemplo prático de uso da API

author: joamatab
body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Expose a new length_extension option in ring couplers and related components, extend coupler90 with a length_straight parameter, refine CLI command options and defaults, and add a full suite of CLI tests while updating regression fixtures.

New Features:
- Expose length_extension parameter (straight length extension at coupler bottom ports) in coupler_ring and make it configurable in ring_single, ring_double, ring_double_heater, ring_single_dut, and ring_single_array components
- Add optional length_straight parameter to coupler90 to customize the straight segment length

Enhancements:
- Refine CLI commands (write-cells, merge-gds, watch, from-updk) to use typer.Option, improve help text, argument parsing, and default path handling
- Bump default spacing between rings in ring_single_array from 5.0 to 15.0
- Simplify ring geometry code by removing redundant type checks and assertion on numpy arrays

Tests:
- Add comprehensive CLI test suite under tests/test_cli.py covering all commands, options, and edge cases

Chores:
- Update test-data-regression YAML fixtures to reflect new parameter names, defaults, and component signatures

author: dinorush
body:
- Added RequireEABAllowed field to BehaviorAbilityCustom to restrict the ability usage if the enemy can't use normal abilities.
- Added StopRootMotion field to DoAnim to restrict animation movement.
- Fixed health-damaging FogCustom only affecting host.
- Fixed EMP and StandStill animations overriding each other and enabling enemy movement early.
- Fixed issues where EMP and StandStill animations could allow enemies to perform actions they shouldn't when interrupted.
- Fixed SpawnProjectiles with "FindTargetIfInvalid" set targeting downed players.
- Enabled LiveEdit by default.

Dev notes:
- StandStill's internal value was changed to an int to track active usages, as the previous boolean type couldn't really support that.
- OnExit is now called before Executing is set to false to allow abilities with StandStill set to revert their state first so `AllowEABAbilityWhileExecuting` can be used correctly.
- Changed SpawnEnemy to use StandStill instead of only stopping their navmesh agent since it seems like StandStill is a more modern approach (was likely added after SpawnEnemy, but I didn't check).
  - On a similar note, I moved the navmesh agent stopping behavior to StandStill to keep everything together.
  - Restoring the stopped agent was mostly removed since switching to PathMove (from exiting StandStill) re-enables it.
- LiveEdit on by default since it's often far more convenient and lighter than HotReload now that it actually works.

author: stanhu
body:
With the switch from Rayon (parallel processing) to Tokio (async) in https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/5172, `mise exec` no longer correctly resolves tool versions if `.tool-versions` contains an unknown entry.

This occurred because a single failure would cause a hard faliure in the `resolve()` method in `src/toolset/mod.rs`. Fix this by setting successful tool resolutions while returning the errors, which can be ignored by the caller.

Relates to https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/5282

- check_dict_comprehension: Flags building a dict inside a loop via repeated d[key] = … assignments, suggesting a dict comprehension.
- check_set_comprehension: Flags using s.add(...) in a loop (instead of a set comprehension).
- check_genexpr_vs_list: Flags calls like sum([ … ]) or any([ … ]) and recommends using generator expressions (sum(…) without the [...]).
- check_membership_on_list_in_loop: Flags x in y or x not in y inside a loop (where y is a Name), recommending converting that list to a set if lookups are frequent.
- check_open_without_context: Flags any call to open() outside of a with …: block, telling the user to switch to a context manager.

author: thusharaj
body:
This feature adds the ability to automatically generate complete, runnable Playwright scripts from agent sessions. The implementation leverages LLM capabilities to transform agent actions into clean, maintainable playwright test automation code.

**Core functionality:**

- Extract and process agent actions (both initial and history actions)
- Transform action data into LLM-friendly format
- Generate complete Playwright scripts via LLM
- Save scripts to output directory with descriptive names
- Mask sensitive data throughout the pipeline

**Key components:**

1. Action extraction system:
- Added extract_playwright_actions method to process agent actions
- Support for initial navigation actions with include_initial_actions parameter
- Proper formatting of action parameters and results
- Conditional JSON output based on debug logging level

2. LLM integration:
- Designed prompt template for Playwright code generation
- Implemented context handling for complex action sequences
- Added support for headless/headed mode configuration
- Ensured sensitive data masking with tags


3. Script management:
- Automatic script naming based on actions and timestamps
- Standardized output directory structure
- Proper file permissions and error handling
- Simplified path handling for better user experience

4. Example implementation:
- Created comprehensive example in playwright-script-generator.py
- Added asyncio handling with proper timeouts and cleanup
- Demonstrated end-to-end workflow from agent creation to script execution
- Included initial actions for complete page navigation

5. Comprehensive test suite:
- Added 12 test cases covering all aspects of the feature
- Test cases for basic action extraction
- Dedicated tests for initial actions handling
- Tests for empty history edge cases
- Tests for debug mode JSON output
- Tests for script generation with various inputs
- Tests for LLM prompt construction
- Tests for script cleanup and path generation
- All tests are async-compatible and use proper mocking

**Technical implementation details:**
- Used Anthropic LLM for script generation via langchain integration
- Implemented proper async/await patterns throughout
- Added signal handling for graceful termination
- Used timeout protection to prevent hanging
- Ensured proper resource cleanup even during interruption
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing agent functionality
- Added type hints and docstrings for better code quality

This feature enables users to easily convert their browser-use agent sessions into reusable Playwright automation scripts, significantly enhancing the tool's utility for testing and automation workflows.

This PR updates [Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django) from **3.2.5** to **5.2.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 5.2.2
   ```
   ==========================

*June 4, 2025*

Django 5.2.2 fixes a security issue with severity "low" and several bugs in
5.2.1.

CVE-2025-48432: Potential log injection via unescaped request path
==================================================================

Internal HTTP response logging used ``request.path`` directly, allowing control
characters (e.g. newlines or ANSI escape sequences) to be written unescaped
into logs. This could enable log injection or forgery, letting attackers
manipulate log appearance or structure, especially in logs processed by
external systems or viewed in terminals.

Although this does not directly impact Django's security model, it poses risks
when logs are consumed or interpreted by other tools. To fix this, the internal
``django.utils.log.log_response()`` function now escapes all positional
formatting arguments using a safe encoding.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a crash when using ``select_related`` against a ``ForeignObject``
  originating from a model with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` (:ticket:`36373`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where subqueries using ``"pk"`` to reference models
  with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` failed to raise ``ValueError`` when too many
  or too few columns were selected (:ticket:`36392`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when no arguments were
  passed into ``QuerySet.union()`` (:ticket:`36388`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 where subclasses of ``RemoteUserMiddleware``
  that had overridden ``process_request()`` were no longer supported
  (:ticket:`36390`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using ``OuterRef``
  in the ``filter`` argument of an ``Aggregate`` expression (:ticket:`36404`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using ``OuterRef``
  in PostgreSQL aggregate functions ``ArrayAgg``, ``StringAgg``, and
  ``JSONBAgg`` (:ticket:`36405`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 where admin's ``filter_horizontal`` buttons
  lacked ``type="button"``, causing them to intercept form submission when
  pressing the Enter key (:ticket:`36423`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where calling ``QuerySet.in_bulk()`` with an
  ``id_list`` argument on models with a ``CompositePrimaryKey`` failed to
  observe database parameter limits (:ticket:`36416`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where :meth:`HttpRequest.get_preferred_type()
  <django.http.HttpRequest.get_preferred_type>` did not account for media type
  parameters in ``Accept`` headers, reducing specificity in content negotiation
  (:ticket:`36411`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using
  ``QuerySet.prefetch_related()`` to prefetch a foreign key with a ``Prefetch``
  queryset for a subclass of the foreign target (:ticket:`36432`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.1
   ```
   ==========================

*May 7, 2025*

Django 5.2.1 fixes a security issue with severity "moderate" and several bugs
in 5.2.

This release was built using an upgraded :pypi:`setuptools`, producing
filenames compliant with :pep:`491` and :pep:`625` and thus addressing a PyPI
warning about non-compliant distribution filenames. This change only affects
the Django packaging process and does not impact Django's behavior.

CVE-2025-32873: Denial-of-service possibility in ``strip_tags()``
=================================================================

:func:`~django.utils.html.strip_tags` would be slow to evaluate certain inputs
containing large sequences of incomplete HTML tags. This function is used to
implement the :tfilter:`striptags` template filter, which was thus also
vulnerable.

:func:`~django.utils.html.strip_tags` now raises a :exc:`.SuspiciousOperation`
exception if it encounters an unusually large number of unclosed opening tags.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when annotating
  aggregate expressions over query that uses explicit grouping by transforms
  followed by field references (:ticket:`36292`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused unnecessary queries when
  prefetching nullable foreign key relationships (:ticket:`36290`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash of
  ``QuerySet.bulk_create()`` with nullable geometry fields on PostGIS
  (:ticket:`36289`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused fields to be incorrectly
  selected when using ``QuerySet.alias()`` after ``values()``
  (:ticket:`36299`).

* Fixed a data corruption possibility in ``file_move_safe()`` when
  ``allow_overwrite=True``, where leftover content from a previously larger
  file could remain after overwriting with a smaller one due to lack of
  truncation (:ticket:`36298`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using
  ``QuerySet.select_for_update(of=(…))`` with ``values()/values_list()``
  including expressions (:ticket:`36301`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused improper values to be returned
  from ``QuerySet.values_list()`` when duplicate field names were specified
  (:ticket:`36288`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 where the password validation error message
  from ``MinimumLengthValidator`` was not translated when using non-English
  locales (:ticket:`36314`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused the ``object-tools`` block to be
  rendered twice when using custom admin templates with overridden blocks due
  to changes in the base admin page block structure (:ticket:`36331`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2, introduced when fixing :cve:`2025-26699`,
  where the :tfilter:`wordwrap` template filter did not preserve empty lines
  between paragraphs after wrapping text (:ticket:`36341`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when serializing email
  alternatives or attachments due to named tuple mismatches (:ticket:`36309`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2 that caused a crash when using ``update()``
  on a ``QuerySet`` filtered against a related model and including references
  to annotations through ``values()`` (:ticket:`36360`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 that caused composite primary key introspection to
  wrongly identify ``IntegerField`` as ``AutoField`` on SQLite
  (:ticket:`36358`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 that caused a redundant ``unique_together``
  constraint to be generated for composite primary keys when using
  :djadmin:`inspectdb` (:ticket:`36357`).

author: frangio
body:
Tags are extracted with extra surrounding spaces and descriptions (the dashes are only there when there is no description). Additionally, the completions are evaluating when the script loads rather than when requested.

This fixes both things.

The awk script first finds the column where `Description` starts, then takes tag rows up to that column and removes trailing spaces.

(Originally in https://github.com/GothenburgBitFactory/timewarrior/pull/673)
